article.title: Turkiye says roadmap being prepared for others to join defence pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia
article.summary: ISTANBUL: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Monday that a roadmap was being worked on for the process of other countries joining the joint defence pact established earlier this month by Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia.Fidan was speaking at a press conference after the first meeting of a key committee established as part of the “Makkah Defence Alliance”, bringing together Muslim US allies concerned by regional conflict. The three countries signed the agreement on August 7 in Saudi Arabia’s Makkah, Islam’s holy city.Turkiye, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan to hold first defence pact meeting tomorrow: FO

article.title: Turkey says regional defence pact not against any country
article.summary: Turkey's top diplomat stressed Monday the regional defence pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia was not aimed at any particular country and open to others, including Egypt.Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan's remarks came after the first ministerial meeting of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement which commits Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia to mutual defence in the event of any of them being attacked.

article.title: Makkah Defence Alliance to be institutionalised, Pakistan to head secretariat for 3 years: FO
article.summary: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye have agreed to further institutionalise their cooperation under the Makkah Agreement to strengthen collective deterrence and defence, with the alliance’s secretariat to be initially headed by Pakistan for three years, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Monday.The decision was taken at the first meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee of the Makkah Agreement, held in Istanbul.Foreign and defence ministers of the three countries, as well as top military officials, attended the meeting in Istanbul’s Ciragan Palace.Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif represented Pakistan.According to the FO, a secretariat headed by a secretary general will be established in Saudi Arabia to support the alliance’s work under the agreement. article.title: Turkey says roadmap being prepared to expand Mecca defence alliance
article.summary: Turkey says roadmap being prepared to expand Mecca defence allianceTurkey is working on a roadmap for other countries to join a joint defence pact established earlier this month with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Monday.Fidan was speaking at a press conference after the first meeting of a key committee established under what has been described as the “Mecca Defence Alliance”.The alliance brings together Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, three predominantly Sunni Muslim countries that are also US partners, amid growing regional security concerns.The three countries signed the defence agreement on 7 August in Mecca, Saudi Arabia. Fidan said work was now under way on a mechanism to allow other countries to join the pact.The announcement comes as regional states reassess their security arrangements amid escalating tensions and conflicts across the Middle East.

article.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan agree to establish secretariat under joint defence pact
article.summary: Aug 31 (Reuters) - Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan agreed to establish a secretariat in Saudi Arabia under their Mecca joint defence agreement, which will initially be headed by a Pakistani secretary-general for three years, the three countries said in a joint statement on Monday.• The three countries' representatives met in Istanbul on Monday.• The countries will work to strengthen their collective defence capabilities and cohesion of their armed forces, the statement said.
